finding.claim: Cached tokens without a numeric iat are served from cache after their exp has passed, bounded only by cacheTTL (default 600000 ms).
finding.source: Attacker holds a validly signed token with exp but no numeric iat, and the verifier has caching enabled (cache: true or a number).
finding.sink: Cache hit at src/verifier.js:377 returns the payload without re-checking exp.

trace.note: First request misses the cache.
verifyToken checks exp (lines 318-322) before caching.
cacheSet called on success.
hasIat is false, so the nbf/exp bound block (120-129) is skipped.
cacheValue initialised to [value, 0, 0].
Upper bound set to clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, not exp.
Later request after exp: min===0 and now<=max, so the cache hits.
handleCachedResult returns the payload; exp is never re-checked.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified before caching (verifier.js:424 precedes 426). exp validator runs only on the uncached path. Cache-hit path has no exp re-check; cacheTTL is the only bound. Caching is opt-in (createCache at verifier.js:580). Related: maxAge bound includes clockTolerance (verifier.js:127) while the validator does not (verifier.js:617).

finding.claim: With an HS-only algorithms allowlist, a serialized public JWK/JWKS passed as key is used as an HMAC secret, bypassing the asymmetric-JWK guard.
finding.source: Operator sets algorithms to HS* only and passes an RSA/EC/OKP public JWK or JWKS JSON as key. The attacker can read that public JSON.
finding.sink: HMAC verification at src/crypto.js:391 using the JWK JSON bytes as the secret.

trace.note: createVerifier calls detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, ['HS256']).
All-HS check returns early, before locatePem and assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson.
checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms passes for HS256.
prepareKeyOrSecret(key, true) calls createSecretKey on the JSON bytes.
Attacker's header alg HS256 is in the allowlist.
HMAC over the JWK JSON bytes verifies the attacker-signed token.

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist (verifier.js:162) permits HS256, so it does not block. assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson (crypto.js:136-139) is skipped on the early-return path. The async path (verifier.js:456) runs the guard and rejects, so sync and async behave inconsistently. Requires operator misconfiguration.

finding.claim: When algorithms is unset, a non-PEM public key (OpenSSH or bare base64 DER) is classified as a raw HMAC secret, so an attacker who knows the public key can forge HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Operator passes a public key without a PEM header (e.g. 'ssh-rsa AAAA...' or bare base64 DER) and omits algorithms. The attacker knows that public key.
finding.sink: HMAC verification at src/crypto.js:391 using the public-key string as the secret.

trace.note: detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, []) is called; early return does not apply (no provided algorithms).
locatePem finds no -----BEGIN header, so isRawSecret is true.
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson only rejects JSON, so the string passes.
Returns hsAlgorithms.
allowedAlgorithms set to HS*.
Public-key string used as the HMAC secret.
Attacker HS256 token signed with the public-key string verifies.

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist is derived from the key, so it accepts HS* for a non-PEM key. PEM detection (crypto.js:158, 223-235) runs only when a header is present. JWK guard (crypto.js:136-139) covers JSON only. Requires operator misconfiguration (algorithms unset).

finding.claim: With caching enabled, a Buffer token throws a plain TypeError from the cache key builder instead of a TokenError.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (e.g. a raw request body) to a verifier with caching enabled.
finding.sink: hashToken calls token.split on a Buffer, throwing TypeError (src/utils.js:46).

trace.note: Type check accepts Buffer tokens.
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) is called before Buffer-to-string conversion.
hashToken calls token.split, which does not exist on a Buffer, so TypeError is thrown.
Buffer-to-string conversion only happens later in the decoder, after the cache lookup.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 accepts Buffers; no normalisation occurs before the cache lookup. Impact is robustness only: non-TokenError exception, thrown synchronously instead of via callback in callback mode. Not an auth bypass.
